original_value: By providing storage and computational resources at the network edge, which enables hosting applications closer to the mobile users, Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) uses the mobile backhaul, and the network core more efficiently, thereby reducing the overall latency. Fostering the synergy between 5G and MEC brings ultra-reliable low-latency in data transmission, and paves the way towards numerous latency-sensitive automotive use cases, with the ultimate goal of enabling autonomous driving. Despite the benefits of significant latency reduction, bringing MEC platforms into 5G-based vehicular networks imposes severe challenges towards poorly scalable network management, as MEC platforms usually represent a highly heterogeneous environment. Therefore, there is a strong need to perform network management and orchestration in an automated way, which, being supported by Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV), will further decrease the latency. With recent advances in SDN, along with NFV, which aim to facilitate management automation for tackling delay issues in vehicular communications, we study the closed-loop life-cycle management of network services, and map such cycle to the Management and Orchestration (MANO) systems, such as ETSI NFV MANO. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive overview of existing MANO solutions, studying their most important features to enable network service and resource orchestration in MEC-enhanced vehicular networks. Finally, using a real testbed setup, we conduct and present an extensive performance analysis of Open Baton and Open Source MANO that are, due to their lightweight resource footprint, and compliance to ETSI standards, suitable solutions for resource and service management and orchestration within the network edge.

result.paraphrase: By supplying storage and compute resources at the network edge, Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) lets applications run closer to mobile users and makes more efficient use of the mobile backhaul and network core, which lowers overall latency. Combining 5G with MEC delivers ultra-reliable low-latency data transmission and opens the door to many latency-sensitive automotive applications, ultimately aiming to support autonomous driving. However, despite the substantial latency gains, deploying MEC platforms in 5G vehicular networks creates major challenges for scalable network management because MEC environments are typically highly heterogeneous. This makes automated network management and orchestration essential; supported by Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV), such automation can further reduce latency. Building on recent advances in SDN and NFV for managing delay in vehicular communications, we examine closed-loop network service life-cycle management and relate it to Management and Orchestration (MANO) frameworks such as ETSI NFV MANO. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of current MANO solutions, focusing on their key features for enabling network service and resource orchestration in MEC-enhanced vehicular networks. Finally, through a real testbed, we perform and report an extensive performance evaluation of Open Baton and Open Source MANO, which are well suited for resource and service management and orchestration at the network edge because of their lightweight resource footprint and ETSI compliance.
